rules.name: sdk-must-not-import-plugins
rules.why: The SDK is public surface for plugin authors and is source-agnostic. If it can import a plugin, every collector inherits that plugin's dependencies and the SDK stops being something a third party can build against alone.

rules.name: sdk-must-not-import-source-clients
rules.why: The SDK is source-agnostic. A source client here would put a Keycloak dependency in the build of every plugin anyone ever writes.

rules.name: contract-module-stays-standalone
rules.why: api/ holds generated contract types. Every collector depends on it, so it must depend on nothing of ours.

rules.name: tools-are-standalone
rules.why: Build tooling must not depend on shipped code, or a broken build becomes a broken linter and the failure is unreadable.

rules.name: plugin-keycloak-does-not-import-other-plugins
rules.why: Each collector is its own module and its own binary. If one imports another, a buyer auditing the Keycloak collector is auditing the GitHub one too, and the two can no longer be released apart. A new collector adds a rule here.

rules.name: plugin-github-does-not-import-other-plugins
rules.why: Each collector is its own module and its own binary. If one imports another, a buyer auditing the Keycloak collector is auditing the GitHub one too, and the two can no longer be released apart. A new collector adds a rule here.

rules.name: plugin-awsiam-does-not-import-other-plugins

rules.name: plugin-entra-does-not-import-other-plugins

rules.name: agent-does-not-import-plugins
rules.why: The agent runs whichever collector binary it is pointed at, as a separate process. If it imports a collector, an auditor reading the agent is reading that collector too, and the agent can no longer be released apart from it.

rules.name: verify-stays-standalone
rules.why: An auditor reads the verifier to decide whether to rely on its answer, so it has to be readable on its own. If it imports anything of ours, they are reading that too, and a change there can change what it accepts. It uses the standard library only.

rules.name: nothing-imports-the-agent
rules.why: The contract, the SDK and the collectors are what an author builds against. If any of them imports the agent, the agent's dependencies become theirs, and a collector can no longer be audited without it.

rules.name: nothing-imports-verify
rules.why: The verifier is released and read apart from the collectors. If the contract, the SDK, a collector or the agent imports it, a change to the verifier changes what that code does, and none of them can be audited without it.
